Subject: PO format & invoicing cadence question for DL-8721

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the recent pricing update — really helpful. Procurement had a quick review and we have two items blocking our AP team before we can issue a formal PO:

1) PO reference: our ERP requires a single line PO number at invoice header and a separate customer account code in the invoice body. Can Redwood accept invoices that include a secondary reference (customer_code) in the invoice body, or do you need PO-only at the header?

2) Invoice cadence vs packaging tiers: We purchase in quarterly capacity packages but our AP prefers weekly statementing to align with internal cashflow. If we buy the quarterly package (Tier C), can Redwood emit weekly invoices/stubs that roll up to the quarterly commitment, or do invoices need to map 1:1 to package tiers?

Attached is our current pricing matrix and the ERP header spec (Procurely_pricing_matrix_v2.xlsx). Any chance you can confirm what you require so we can prepare the PO correctly? Also include what net terms Redwood can offer for DL-8721 — our standard is Net45 but we can negotiate.

Appreciate a short note or a quick 20-min call.

Best,
Sara

Subject: Re: PO format & invoicing cadence question for DL-8721

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear note and the matrix. Quick answers to get you unstuck, then we can lock details on a call: 

- PO/reference: We can accept the PO number in the invoice header and include an additional customer_code field in the invoice body (we add it as an invoice-level custom field). Our billing system will map both for AP reconciliation. Please instruct AP to include both in the invoice PDF and the EDI/XML payload.

- Invoice cadence v. packaging: We can support weekly invoice stubs that roll up to a quarterly commitment for accounting purposes (so you'll see weekly amounts, but the usage is counted against the quarterly package). Two caveats: weekly stubs are travel-light (summary lines) — detailed itemization will be quarterly. Also, for true prepaid packages where payment is taken up front, we recommend a single quarterly invoice; for committed usage with monthly billing, weekly stubs are fine.

- Net terms: Standard offered is Net30 for new customers on hosted plans. For DL-8721 (Procurely), we can extend Net45 if there is an approved signed commitment (volume/term). Vanessa, can you confirm if finance needs a signed order form to commit Net45?

I can jump on a call Mon morning if that works for you.

—Michael
Michael Grant
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO format & invoicing cadence question for DL-8721

Hi Sara — looping in AP/Finance context. Short answers from finance: 

- Net45: Finance can approve Net45 for DL-8721 on a signed order with an explicit quarterly committed spend line item. We need the signed order and the PO to reference the deal id (DL-8721) and the billing BU code.

- Invoice layout: We require the PO number in the header and the customer_code field populated in the invoice body as Michael suggested. For EDI/ERP, we prefer CSV/EDIFACT payloads but will accept PDF invoices paired with a CSV summary.

- Weekly stubs: Acceptable as long as the invoice total reconciles to the quarterly commitment and you include a deterministic usage-sum line each week. If there are credits/refunds, those must be issued as separate credit memos and reference the original PO.

I attached our packaging tiers doc so you can see mapping suggestions: Redwood_packaging_tiers_v1.pdf

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Revenue Finance | Redwood Inference

Thanks Michael/Vanessa — that helps. A couple of follow-ups: 

- Our AR system prefers the weekly stub to include a 'period_to_date' balance so the AP team can reconcile against the quarterly commitment automatically. Is that something Redwood can populate in the CSV summary?

- On Net45: procurement will get the signed order signed by our CFO once we validate the PO format and weekly stub. Are there any discount implications if we take quarterly prepay vs committed quarterly billed with Net45? Procurely is evaluating a 12-month commitment but the pricing bands differ for prepaid vs committed-billed.

Can you confirm discount behavior per packaging tier (example: Tier B 6-month commit vs Tier B prepaid) — are discounts additive or are they distinct pricing tables? I attached a redline to the pricing matrix with our expected structure.

If it's easier, we can schedule 20 minutes today 1:30pm PT. Tom and I are available.

Best,
Sara

Sara / Tom — thanks. Quick clarifications before the 1:30pm call: 

- period_to_date: yes, we can include period_to_date and cumulative committed usage in the CSV stub. We'll add a 'committed_balance' column that shows remaining committed units/value for the quarter.

- discount model: discounts are per-pricing table (prepay vs committed-billed). They are not additive. Prepay pricing uses a separate (more aggressive) discount table; committed-billed (Net45) uses the committed discount table which depends on term length and volume. For a 12-month commitment we can move Procurely into the Q12 band; exact tiering will depend on uplift thresholds (Ben, I'll hand this to you to confirm the uplift breakpoints for Tier B -> Q12).

Action items before call (short):
- Redwood (Ben): confirm uplift breakpoints & send final committed-billing price table.
- Redwood (Michael/Vanessa): prepare sample weekly CSV stub showing period_to_date and committed_balance.
- Procurely (Sara): share final target package (prepay vs committed) and confirm availability for 1:30pm PT.

I'll send a calendar invite; talk shortly.

—Michael
